notes_for_adoption: This taxonomy categorizes social media hooks for use in content creation tools. Use 'regex_triggers' to provide real-time suggestions on script drafts. Use 'warnings' to power a linter or helper tool for creators.

emotional.name: Emotional Hooks (Targeting Affect)
emotional.description: Hooks that aim to elicit an immediate and strong emotional response.

hooks.name: Provocation & Controversy
hooks.description: Starting with a deliberately divisive or challenging statement (a 'hot take') that opposes a common belief.
examples: You're building your business all wrong.
Unpopular opinion: [Commonly loved thing] is overrated.
Stop doing this if you want to succeed.
warnings: High risk of attracting negative comments.
Can alienate parts of your audience.
May damage brand reputation if overused or inauthentic.

hooks.name: Empathy & Vulnerability
hooks.description: Showing raw, unfiltered emotion or admitting a personal failure or secret.
examples: Storytime: The moment I got fired.
I have to tell you something...
My biggest failure...
regex_triggers: /(i got fired|i failed|my biggest failure|my biggest regret)/i
/(i need to be honest|a secret about|i'm embarrassed to admit)/i
warnings: Requires genuine vulnerability; can backfire if perceived as fake.
Risk of oversharing personal details.
Can be emotionally draining to create.

hooks.name: Outrage & Injustice
hooks.description: Tapping into a shared sense of frustration or a perceived injustice; often framed as a 'rant'.
examples: They are lying to you about...
I can't be the only one who's sick of this.
This is a total scam.
regex_triggers: /(they are lying|it's a lie|is a scam)/i
/(i can't be the only one|am i the only one)/i
/(i'm sick of|i hate this|this is unacceptable)/i
warnings: Fosters negativity and polarized audiences.
Can be factually inaccurate if based purely on emotion.
Risk of being seen as a 'complainer'.

cognitive.name: Cognitive & Curiosity Hooks
cognitive.description: Hooks that pose a question or create an information gap that the viewer feels compelled to resolve.

hooks.name: The Knowledge Gap
hooks.description: Implying the viewer is missing crucial or secret information.
examples: This is the one secret to [Goal] that no one is talking about.
You won't believe what I just found out.
Here's why you're always tired.
regex_triggers: /(what no one tells you|what they don't want you to know)/i
warnings: Classic clickbait; can annoy users if the payoff isn't good.
Must deliver on the 'secret' or lose trust.

hooks.name: The Pattern Interrupt
hooks.description: Starting *in media res* (in the middle of the action) or with a non-sequitur that breaks scrolling hypnosis.
examples: [Starts mid-sentence]
[Throws object at camera]
[Bizarre or out-of-context opening shot]
warnings: Can be confusing if not resolved quickly.
Relies heavily on strong editing or performance.
May not be suitable for all topics.
hooks.notes_for_devs: This hook is often detected by analyzing video/audio (e.g., sudden scene change, loud noise at t=0, or unusual grammar) rather than just text.

hooks.name: The Quantified Promise (Listicle)
hooks.description: Promising a specific, digestible number of insights or tips.
examples: 3 ways to fix your sleep schedule.
The #1 mistake people make when...
5 apps I can't live without.
warnings: Can feel generic or low-effort.
The content must match the number promised and deliver real value for each point.

sensory.name: Sensory Hooks
sensory.description: Hooks that use satisfying or jarring audio-visual stimuli to create a physical or sensory reaction.

hooks.name: ASMR
hooks.description: Using quiet, 'tingly' sounds like whispering, tapping, or crinkling.
examples: [Whispering]
[Tapping on mic]
[Crinkling paper]
warnings: Niche audience; can be unpleasant for those who dislike ASMR.
Requires a high-quality microphone and controlled recording environment.
hooks.notes_for_devs: Best detected by audio analysis (low decibels, specific frequencies) combined with text triggers.

hooks.name: Oddly Satisfying
hooks.description: Showing perfect processes, symmetry, transformation, or clean destruction.
examples: [Paint mixing]
[Kinetic sand cutting]
[Hydraulic press]
[Perfect handwriting]
warnings: Relies 100% on high-quality, stable visuals.
Can be very time-consuming to film and set up.
hooks.notes_for_devs: Primarily a visual-only hook. Text triggers are often in the description, not the hook itself.

hooks.name: Dynamic Motion
hooks.description: Using fast camera movements, a dramatic physical action, or rapid cuts to grab the eye.
examples: [Camera 'swoosh']
[Dropping an item]
[Fast-paced editing]
warnings: Can be disorienting if overdone.
Requires good editing skills.
hooks.notes_for_devs: Primarily a video editing technique. Hard to detect from text alone.

social.name: Social & Relational Hooks
social.description: Hooks that leverage social psychology, making the viewer feel part of (or against) a group.

hooks.name: The 'Relatability' Hook (POV)
hooks.description: Naming a highly specific, shared experience or feeling, often using 'POV' (Point of View).
examples: POV: You're trying to work but your cat...
It's that feeling when...
Things only [Group] will understand.
warnings: Can feel exclusive if the 'shared' experience is too niche.
Relies on deep audience understanding.
Risk of being unoriginal.

hooks.name: The 'Authority' Hook (Social Proof)
hooks.description: Immediately establishing credibility or expertise to make the information seem valuable.
examples: As a doctor with 15 years of experience...
What I learned from interviewing 100 millionaires...
As a former [Big Tech Company] employee...
warnings: Requires genuine credentials or it's fraudulent.
Can sound arrogant if not handled carefully.
Must be relevant to the content.

hooks.name: The 'Us vs. Them' Hook (Conflict)
hooks.description: Creating a binary opposition or perceived conflict between two groups, forcing the viewer to 'pick a side'.
examples: There are two types of people in this world...
Millennials vs. Gen Z try...
Why [Group A] is better than [Group B].
regex_triggers: /(two types of people|2 types of people)/i
warnings: Can create unnecessary division and negativity.
Oversimplifies complex issues.
Risks alienating the 'losing' side.

utility.name: Utility & Value Hooks
utility.description: Hooks that make an explicit promise that the content will solve a problem or provide a direct benefit.

hooks.name: Problem-Solution
hooks.description: Stating a common problem and immediately promising the solution.
examples: If you struggle with [Problem], you need to do this one thing.
Stop doing [Common Mistake], do this instead.
Your [Item] keeps dying? Here's how to fix it.
regex_triggers: /(if you struggle with|do you struggle with|tired of)/i
/(here's how to fix|how to solve|do this instead)/i
warnings: The solution must be clear, concise, and valuable.
The problem must be one the audience actually has.
Can sound 'salesy' if not genuine.

hooks.name: The 'Hack' / Shortcut
hooks.description: Promising a faster, cheaper, or easier way to accomplish a task.
examples: The easiest way to clean [Object].
How to get [Expensive Item] for free.
I'm going to teach you [Skill] in 30 seconds.
regex_triggers: /(easiest way to|quickest way to|fastest way to)/i
warnings: The 'hack' must actually work and be a true shortcut.
Can devalue expertise if all content is 'hacks'.
May border on clickbait if the promise is exaggerated.

hooks.name: The Direct Promise
hooks.description: Clearly and directly stating what the viewer will gain by watching.
examples: By the end of this video, you will know how to...
I'm going to show you exactly how to set up...
This video will teach you...
warnings: Very straightforward; may not be 'flashy' enough for all platforms.
You MUST deliver 100% on the promise or you will lose credibility.
